Read whole files with the Read tool (paging sequentially through large files is fine). A hook enforces this.\n\n## The problem, with measured evidence\n\nESBMC's counterexample values are used to generate Foundry tests (`--generate-foundry-testcase`). Some model values CANNOT be replayed on a real chain. Two distinct classes, and the second is the dangerous one:\n\n(a) NOT RENDERABLE — the value is not a concrete scalar. Measured, verbatim, from a real counterexample on the `farming` benchmark:\n```\nstakingToken_ = INVALID-2\nrewardsToken_ = INVALID-2\nname_         = (signed char *)0x...F\n._name        = &dynamic_1_array[0]\n._ESBMC_bind_cname = { .pointer_object=nil, .pointer_offset=nil }\n```\n\n(b) RENDERABLE BUT ILLEGAL OR SEMANTICALLY WRONG ON CHAIN — the value is a perfectly concrete constant, so every \"is it concrete?\" check passes, and it still produces a test that is RED on the unmodified contract. Measured in the same counterexample:\n```\nmsg_sender     = 0\ntx_origin      = 0\nblock_coinbase = 0\n```\n`address(0)` cannot originate a transaction, and a large fraction of real contracts contain `require(msg.sender != address(0))` or equivalent. There is already a regression directory named `regression/esbmc-solidity/foundry_covgen_msgsender_not_pinned_knownbug`, which suggests this has been hit before and left as a known bug.\n\n## Your task\n\nAudit the emission path and answer these questions with file:line evidence:\n\n1. Where are counterexample values harvested into `goto_coveraget::path_ce_t` (fields `inputs`, `env`, `entry_storage`, `final_state`)? The header comment claims \"Both are recorded ONLY from concrete model values; a symbolic or missing value is dropped rather than guessed.\" VERIFY that claim against the code. What exactly is the concreteness test, and what happens to a value that fails it — is it dropped, defaulted, or rendered anyway?\n\n2. **The key question.** When an input is DROPPED by that test, what does the Foundry emitter put in its place in the generated test? Trace it: `src/goto-symex/foundry.cpp` and `foundry.h`. If it substitutes a default (0, address(0), empty bytes) then a dropped value becomes a SILENT wrong test — the test compiles, runs, and exercises a different input than the counterexample. Say definitively whether this happens, and name the line.\n\n3. Does anything in the emitter reject a case whose values are illegal on chain (`msg.sender == address(0)`, a contract-typed argument with no deployable address, `block.timestamp == 0`, etc.)? If nothing does, say so plainly.\n\n4. Read `regression/esbmc-solidity/foundry_covgen_msgsender_not_pinned_knownbug/` in full (contract + test.desc + any generated .sol) and report exactly what it pins and what it says the known bug is.\n\n5. There is an existing precedent for the right shape of fix in this codebase: the NAMED OBSTACLE mechanism. Read the comment on `named_obstacle_paths` in `src/goto-programs/goto_coverage.h` and the refusal in `src/goto-symex/foundry.cpp` (search by reading the file; it counts refused cases in a `suppressed_obstacle` counter and prints a warning BEFORE the empty-check in `generate()`). Summarise that shape in three sentences: mark, exclude, and COUNT ON STDOUT.\n\n## Output\n\nA markdown report with:\n- a table of every place a CE value can be lost or replaced, with file:line and what the consumer sees;\n- a plain verdict on question 2 (does a dropped input become a defaulted value in the emitted test — yes or no, with the line);\n- a proposed fix, following the named-obstacle shape: what to detect, where to refuse, what counter and what stdout line, and how a regression test would fault-inject it so that disabling the refusal turns exactly one test red.\n- Anything you could not settle by reading: mark \"UNVERIFIED\" and name the file that would settle it. Do not guess.\n\nReturn the report as your final message."},"uuid":"32afbcb9-9106-44af-abf6-06bf86ab3454","timestamp":"2026-07-30T17:48:15.253Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/samson/workspace/paper_review","sessionId":"e0047351-2714-4000-919d-058ca8af97c5","version":"2.1.220","gitBranch":"VeriPUT","slug":"synchronous-wondering-flame"}

{"parentUuid":"46b9a42e-4434-404e-ad0c-fbfeb7b84e90","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"b4a098c7-255e-4b6b-abed-2c1005a4327d","agentId":"a54732ec6678522be","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01YChX2eKK7XoVtS9mtTnCzP","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# msg.sender pinning on a contract that also makes value transfers\n2\t\n3\t## What this test pins\n4\t\n5\tCityToken guards `setCEO` / `setCOO` / `createToken` / `payout` /\n6\t`withdrawFunds` with modifiers that do `require(msg.sender == ceoAddress)`,\n7\t`require(msg.sender == cooAddress)` or the `onlyCLevel` disjunction. ESBMC\n8\tcovers the authorised (guard-true) side of each, so the generated Foundry test\n9\tmust pin `msg.sender` with `vm.prank(...)` — otherwise the replay calls arrive\n10\tfrom the test contract, every guarded call reverts, and the authorised branch\n11\tis reported covered while no test actually reaches it.\n12\t\n13\tThe three `^  !\\(!\\(...\\)\\)` regexes are the authorised arms in the\n14\t`--branch-coverage-claims` reached list; the `vm.prank` line proves the\n15\tgenerator reproduced the sender that reaches them. Counts are matched loosely\n16\t(`[0-9]+`): the exact number of cases follows the solver's model choices, and\n17\tthe \"N call(s) with pinned msg.sender\" line is only printed when N > 0, so a\n18\tzero-pin regression cannot match it.\n19\t\n20\t## The bug this covers (fixed)\n21\t\n22\t`foundry_generator::reconstruct` refused to pin the sender whenever any SSA\n23\tstep assigned the `msg_sender` global outside the per-tx reseed, on the theory\n24\tthat a nested/high/low-level call wrapper had overwritten it and a top-level\n25\t`vm.prank` could no longer reproduce what the covered branch read.\n26\t\n27\tThat test was syntactic, and symex does not preserve the syntax: an assignment\n28\tthat occurs under a branch is merged into an *unconditional* SSA step whose RHS\n29\tis `cond ? new_value : old_value`. Every `$transfer` / `$send` / `$call`\n30\twrapper in the contract therefore shows up as a guard-true `msg_sender` write\n31\ton *every* path — including paths that never enter it. One `.transfer()`\n32\tanywhere in the contract was enough to suppress the pin for all 29 cases,\n33\tincluding `setCEO`, which makes no call at all.\n34\t\n35\tThe fix decides on the *model value* instead: a write that leaves `msg_sender`\n36\tequal to the transaction's top-level sender (an untaken-branch merge, or the\n37\twrapper's own restore on the way out) does not shadow it. Only a read taken\n38\twhile the value genuinely differs marks the segment un-pinnable — which is what\n39\tthe original comment intended.\n40\t\n41\tThis is why the defect did not reproduce on the minimal variants tried\n42\t(inline `require(msg.sender == owner)`, a single-comparison modifier, a mutable\n43\towner, a ctor-bound owner, an inherited guard variable): none of them contained\n44\ta value transfer, so no wrapper existed to poison the path.\n45\t\n46\t## Replay shape\n47\t\n48\tThe generator emits two test contracts, one per deployer identity the solver\n49\tpicked (`CityTokenCovTest_0` deploys under `vm.startPrank(address(0))`,\n50\t`CityTokenCovTest_1` under `vm.startPrank(address(uint160(4294967295)))`).\n51\tWithin each group the calls pranked with that group's deployer exercise the\n52\tauthorised arm and the others the reverting arm, so both sides of every\n53\taccess-control branch have a reaching test.\n54\t"}]},"uuid":"5f5ae326-5114-463f-a7a0-79426db39766","timestamp":"2026-07-30T17:48:29.247Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/samson/workspace/esbmc/regression/esbmc-solidity/foundry_covgen_msgsender_not_pinned_knownbug/NOTES.md","content":"# msg.sender pinning on a contract that also makes value transfers\n\n## What this test pins\n\nCityToken guards `setCEO` / `setCOO` / `createToken` / `payout` /\n`withdrawFunds` with modifiers that do `require(msg.sender == ceoAddress)`,\n`require(msg.sender == cooAddress)` or the `onlyCLevel` disjunction. ESBMC\ncovers the authorised (guard-true) side of each, so the generated Foundry test\nmust pin `msg.sender` with `vm.prank(...)` — otherwise the replay calls arrive\nfrom the test contract, every guarded call reverts, and the authorised branch\nis reported covered while no test actually reaches it.\n\nThe three `^  !\\(!\\(...\\)\\)` regexes are the authorised arms in the\n`--branch-coverage-claims` reached list; the `vm.prank` line proves the\ngenerator reproduced the sender that reaches them. Counts are matched loosely\n(`[0-9]+`): the exact number of cases follows the solver's model choices, and\nthe \"N call(s) with pinned msg.sender\" line is only printed when N > 0, so a\nzero-pin regression cannot match it.\n\n## The bug this covers (fixed)\n\n`foundry_generator::reconstruct` refused to pin the sender whenever any SSA\nstep assigned the `msg_sender` global outside the per-tx reseed, on the theory\nthat a nested/high/low-level call wrapper had overwritten it and a top-level\n`vm.prank` could no longer reproduce what the covered branch read.\n\nThat test was syntactic, and symex does not preserve the syntax: an assignment\nthat occurs under a branch is merged into an *unconditional* SSA step whose RHS\nis `cond ? new_value : old_value`. Every `$transfer` / `$send` / `$call`\nwrapper in the contract therefore shows up as a guard-true `msg_sender` write\non *every* path — including paths that never enter it. One `.transfer()`\nanywhere in the contract was enough to suppress the pin for all 29 cases,\nincluding `setCEO`, which makes no call at all.\n\nThe fix decides on the *model value* instead: a write that leaves `msg_sender`\nequal to the transaction's top-level sender (an untaken-branch merge, or the\nwrapper's own restore on the way out) does not shadow it. Only a read taken\nwhile the value genuinely differs marks the segment un-pinnable — which is what\nthe original comment intended.\n\nThis is why the defect did not reproduce on the minimal variants tried\n(inline `require(msg.sender == owner)`, a single-comparison modifier, a mutable\nowner, a ctor-bound owner, an inherited guard variable): none of them contained\na value transfer, so no wrapper existed to poison the path.\n\n## Replay shape\n\nThe generator emits two test contracts, one per deployer identity the solver\npicked (`CityTokenCovTest_0` deploys under `vm.startPrank(address(0))`,\n`CityTokenCovTest_1` under `vm.startPrank(address(uint160(4294967295)))`).\nWithin each group the calls pranked with that group's deployer exercise the\nauthorised arm and the others the reverting arm, so both sides of every\naccess-control branch have a reaching test.\n","numLines":54,"startLine":1,"totalLines":54}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"46b9a42e-4434-404e-ad0c-fbfeb7b84e90","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/samson/workspace/paper_review","sessionId":"e0047351-2714-4000-919d-058ca8af97c5","version":"2.1.220","gitBranch":"VeriPUT","slug":"synchronous-wondering-flame"}

This\n/// generator reconstructs the transaction sequence from those assignments and\n/// emits a compilable Foundry test that replays it, mirroring the\n/// ctest/pytest generators used for C/Python.\nclass foundry_generator\n{\nprivate:\n  /// One reconstructed argument: its Solidity source type (from the\n  /// `#sol_type` irep on the parameter symbol) and the formatted literal.\n  struct sol_arg\n  {\n    std::string param;    // parameter name\n    std::string sol_type; // e.g. \"UINT256\", \"ADDRESS\", \"BOOL\"\n    std::string literal;  // Solidity literal text, or empty if unformattable\n    expr2tc value;        // raw recovered value (nil if not recovered)\n    // Interface-arg mock synthesis: when this argument is an interface/abstract\n    // contract handle (`#sol_type: CONTRACT`), `mock_iface` names the interface\n    // and a deployed `ESBMCMock_<iface>` instance is passed instead of a\n    // literal. `mock_key` (the parameter name) gives each interface argument its\n    // OWN mock instance (fresh-per-slot), so two handles a constructor forces\n    // distinct (`a != b`) get distinct deployed addresses. That bareness IS the assertion: a revert at run time\n    // fails the test. Distinct from `!reverts`, which until now meant only\n    // \"not confirmed to revert\" and was emitted revert-tolerantly, i.e. with no\n    // assertion at all.\n    //\n    // The three states must stay three. Collapsing \"confirmed normal\" into\n    // \"not confirmed to revert\" is what made every generated test\n    // assertion-free, and collapsing \"not confirmed\" into \"normal\" would assert\n    // that a reverting transaction succeeded. Only complete-path coverage\n    // supplies the distinction (goto_coveraget's revert / rollback_revert /\n    // undetermined_exit sets); branch coverage has no third state and leaves\n    // this false, keeping its output byte-identical.\n    bool normal_confirmed = false;\n    // This call's covered path is a NAMED OBSTACLE: the model admits an\n    // execution the chain does not have, so the counterexample behind it may\n    // describe something that cannot happen and a test built from it is RED on\n    // the UNMODIFIED contract.\n    //\n    // goto_coverage.h states the rule outright -- \"a marked path ... must not be\n    // turned into a test. Marking without excluding would be worthless\" -- and\n    // the marking half was the only half implemented. Test cases are\n  /// grouped by construction signature: each distinct construction becomes its\n  /// own `contract <primary>CovTest[_n] is Test` with a `setUp()` that deploys\n  /// the instance, and the cases sharing it become its `test_cov_*` functions.\n  /// Returns the number of calls wrapped in revert-tolerant try/catch.\n  size_t write_foundry_file(\n    const std::string &path,\n    const std::string &primary,\n    const std::vector<test_case> &cases) const;\n\npublic:\n  foundry_generator() = default;\n\n  /// Clear collected data (start of a coverage run).\n  void clear();\n\n  /// Collect one counterexample (called per reached goal in coverage mode).\n  void collect(\n    const symex_target_equationt &target,\n    smt_convt &smt_conv,\n    const namespacet &ns);\n\n  /// Emit the accumulated test suite.\n  void generate() const;\n\n  /// Single-shot emission for non-coverage mode.\n  void generate_single(\n    const symex_target_equationt &target,\n    smt_convt &smt_conv,\n    const namespacet &ns);\n\n  /// Whether any test case has been collected.\n  bool has_tests() const;\n};\n\n#endif\n","numLines":341,"startLine":1,"totalLines":341}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c8e28a8b-abab-4c36-830e-a0b286c589b1","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/samson/workspace/paper_review","sessionId":"e0047351-2714-4000-919d-058ca8af97c5","version":"2.1.220","gitBranch":"VeriPUT","slug":"synchronous-wondering-flame"}

Locals/temporaries carry extra `@`, contract fields do not\n59\t  // reach here (they are not `@F@`-scoped).\n60\t  if (\n61\t    param.empty() || param.find('@') != std::string::npos || contract.empty() ||\n62\t    method.empty())\n63\t    return false;\n64\t  return true;\n65\t}\n66\t\n67\t// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n68\t// Value formatting\n69\t// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n70\t\n71\tnamespace\n72\t{\n73\t// The effective Solidity type string of a lowered parameter *type*. A fixed\n74\t// bytesN lowers to the `BytesStatic` struct (its `#sol_type` is the tag\n75\t// \"BytesStatic\"); when the source width survives as `#sol_bytesn_size`\n76\t// (set in get_elementary_type_name, solidity_convert_type.cpp) it is recovered\n77\t// as \"BYTES<N>\" so the value formatter can render the exact-width literal. All\n78\t// other types pass their `#sol_type` through unchanged. Surface it so a string call-argument is rendered as a\n112\t    // Solidity string literal reconstructed from the counterexample length\n113\t    // (see format_sol_value / reconstruct's recovered_str_len) instead of being\n114\t    // dropped as unsupported.\n115\t    if (ptag == \"STRING\")\n116\t      return \"STRING\";\n117\t  }\n118\t  // A `bytes` value lowers to the `BytesDynamic` struct (tag \"struct\n119\t  // BytesDynamic\", no #sol_type). NOT \"BytesStatic\" (a fixed bytesN, rendered\n120\t  // from its width elsewhere).\n121\t  if (\n122\t    t.is_struct() &&\n123\t    t.tag().as_string().find(\"BytesDynamic\") != std::string::npos)\n124\t    return \"BYTES_DYN\";\n125\t\n126\t  const typet &ty = t.is_pointer() ? t.subtype() : t;\n127\t  // A fixed bytesN carries its width as `#sol_bytesn_size`. Returns N, or 0 if `sol_type` is not a fixed bytesN.\n154\tunsigned parse_fixed_bytes_width(const std::string &sol_type)\n155\t{\n156\t  if (!has_prefix(sol_type, \"BYTES\") || sol_type.size() <= 5)\n157\t    return 0;\n158\t  if (!std::isdigit(static_cast<unsigned char>(sol_type[5])))\n159\t    return 0;\n160\t  unsigned n = static_cast<unsigned>(std::stoul(sol_type.substr(5)));\n161\t  return (n >= 1 && n <= 32) ? n : 0;\n162\t}\n163\t\n164\t// Render a `bytesN` value recovered from the model as a Solidity literal\n165\t// `bytesN(0x..)`. bytesN is modeled as a BytesStatic struct\n166\t// { unsigned char data[32]; size_t length; } with `data` big-endian\n167\t// (data[0] = most-significant byte; see bytes_static_from_uint), which is\n168\t// exactly how solc lays out a bytesN literal, so emitting data[0..N-1] as hex\n169\t// round-trips to the same 32-byte value. Returns \"\" if the struct/array shape\n170\t// is not a fully-concrete constant.\n171\tstd::string format_fixed_bytes(unsigned n, const expr2tc &value)\n172\t{\n173\t  if (!is_constant_struct2t(value))\n174\t    return \"\";\n175\t  const constant_struct2t &st = to_constant_struct2t(value);\n176\t  if (st.datatype_members.empty())\n177\t    return \"\";\n178\t  const expr2tc &data = st.datatype_members[0]; // the `data[32]` array\n179\t  if (!data) // an unconstrained (e.g. nested-struct) bytesN member — degrade\n180\t    return \"\";\n181\t\n182\t  static const char *hexd = \"0123456789abcdef\";\n183\t  std::string hex;\n184\t  auto append_byte = [&hex](const expr2tc &e) -> bool {\n185\t    if (!is_constant_int2t(e))\n186\t      return false;\n187\t    unsigned b =\n188\t      static_cast<unsigned>(to_constant_int2t(e).value.to_uint64() & 0xffu);\n189\t    hex.push_back(hexd[(b >> 4) & 0xf]);\n190\t    hex.push_back(hexd[b & 0xf]);\n191\t    return true;\n192\t  };\n193\t\n194\t  if (is_constant_array2t(data))\n195\t  {\n196\t    const constant_array2t &arr = to_constant_array2t(data);\n197\t    for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; ++i)\n198\t    {\n199\t      if (\n200\t        i >= arr.datatype_members.size() ||\n201\t        !append_byte(arr.datatype_members[i]))\n202\t        return \"\";\n203\t    }\n204\t  }\n205\t  else if (is_constant_array_of2t(data))\n206\t  {\n207\t    // Whole array collapsed to one repeated element (e.g. all-zero).\n208\t    const expr2tc &init = to_constant_array_of2t(data).initializer;\n209\t    for (unsigned i = 0; i < n; ++i)\n210\t      if (!append_byte(init))\n211\t        return \"\";\n212\t  }\n213\t  else\n214\t    return \"\";\n215\t\n216\t  return \"bytes\" + std::to_string(n) + \"(0x\" + hex + \")\";\n217\t}\n218\t\n219\t// Effective sol-type string of a code_typet argument. Prefers the fixed-bytes\n220\t// width stamped directly on the argument (`#sol_bytesn_size`, set in\n221\t// get_function_params) — this is the authoritative source-declared width and\n222\t// survives the type migration that strips it from the argument *type*. Falls\n223\t// back to the argument type's own tags. `arg` is a code_typet::argumentt\n224\t// (an exprt subtype), so both the direct irep and its type are queryable.\n225\tstd::string arg_sol_type(const exprt &arg)\n226\t{\n227\t  std::string base;\n228\t  const std::string bn = arg.get(\"#sol_bytesn_size\").as_string();\n229\t  if (!bn.empty() && bn.find_first_not_of(\"0123456789\") == std::string::npos)\n230\t  {\n231\t    unsigned n = static_cast<unsigned>(std::stoul(bn));\n232\t    if (n >= 1 && n <= 32)\n233\t      base = \"BYTES\" + std::to_string(n);\n234\t  }\n235\t  // No direct bytesN width stamp: effective_sol_type already applies any UDVT.\n236\t  if (base.empty())\n237\t    return effective_sol_type(arg.type());\n238\t  // A bytesN width was stamped directly on the argument (see\n239\t  // solidity_convert_stmt.cpp). Still apply a UDVT wrapper when the parameter\n240\t  // is a user-defined value type over bytesN, so we emit `Name.wrap(...)`\n241\t  // rather than a bare bytesN literal (not assignable to the UDVT parameter).\n242\t  // The UDVT name is likewise stamped on the argument (the bytesN->BytesStatic\n243\t  // migration drops it from the type), so read it from the argument first.\n244\t  std::string udvt = arg.get(\"#sol_udvt_name\").as_string();\n245\t  if (udvt.empty())\n246\t  {\n247\t    const typet &ty =\n248\t      arg.type().is_pointer() ? arg.type().subtype() : arg.type();\n249\t    udvt = ty.get(\"#sol_udvt_name\").as_string();\n250\t  }\n251\t  return udvt.empty() ? base : \"UDVT:\" + udvt + \":\" + base;\n252\t}\n253\t\n254\t// Solidity source type name for a `#sol_type` string, used to render array\n255\t// element types (`new <name>[](N)`). Returns \"\" for a type we cannot name.\n257\tstd::string sol_type_to_solidity(const std::string &st)\n258\t{\n259\t  if (has_prefix(st, \"ARRAY:\"))\n260\t  {\n261\t    const std::string e = sol_type_to_solidity(st.substr(6));\n262\t    return e.empty() ? \"\" : e + \"[]\";\n263\t  }\n264\t  if (has_prefix(st, \"UDVT:\"))\n265\t  {\n266\t    const std::string rest = st.substr(5);\n267\t    return rest.substr(0, rest.find(':')); // the UDVT name is itself a type\n268\t  }\n269\t  if (st == \"ADDRESS\" || st == \"ADDRESS_PAYABLE\")\n270\t    return \"address\";\n271\t  if (st == \"BOOL\")\n272\t    return \"bool\";\n273\t  if (has_prefix(st, \"UINT\"))\n274\t    return \"uint\" + (st.size() > 4 ? st.substr(4) : std::string(\"256\"));\n275\t  if (has_prefix(st, \"INT\"))\n276\t    return \"int\" + (st.size() > 3 ? st.substr(3) : std::string(\"256\"));\n277\t  if (unsigned n = parse_fixed_bytes_width(st))\n278\t    return \"bytes\" + std::to_string(n);\n279\t  if (st == \"BYTES_DYN\")\n280\t    return \"bytes\";\n281\t  if (st == \"STRING\")\n282\t    return \"string\";\n283\t  return \"\";\n284\t}\n285\t} // namespace\n286\t\n287\tstd::string foundry_generator::format_sol_value(\n288\t  const std::string &sol_type,\n289\t  const expr2tc &value)\n290\t{\n291\t  // User-defined value type \"UDVT:<Name>:<underlying>\": render the underlying\n292\t  // literal, then wrap it (`Name.wrap(<literal>)`) — the only assignable form.\n293\t  if (has_prefix(sol_type, \"UDVT:\"))\n294\t  {\n295\t    const std::string rest = sol_type.substr(5);\n296\t    size_t sep = rest.find(':');\n297\t    if (sep == std::string::npos)\n298\t      return \"\";\n299\t    const std::string name = rest.substr(0, sep);\n300\t    const std::string inner = format_sol_value(rest.substr(sep + 1), value);\n301\t    return inner.empty() ? \"\" : name + \".wrap(\" + inner + \")\";\n302\t  }\n303\t\n304\t  if (sol_type == \"BOOL\")\n305\t  {\n306\t    if (is_constant_bool2t(value))\n307\t      return to_constant_bool2t(value).value ? \"true\" : \"false\";\n308\t    if (is_constant_int2t(value))\n309\t      return (to_constant_int2t(value).value != 0) ? \"true\" : \"false\";\n310\t    return \"\";\n311\t  }\n312\t\n313\t  // Fixed-size bytesN (bytes1..bytes32): recovered as a BytesStatic struct.\n314\t  // The width N MUST come from the declared source type (`#sol_type` =\n315\t  // \"BYTES<N>\"); we never infer it from the recovered struct's `.length`, which\n316\t  // is a free nondet value on any path that does not constrain the bytesN and\n317\t  // could otherwise yield a wrong-width literal for the declared parameter. If\n318\t  // the caller cannot supply the declared width, the value degrades to \"\" (the\n319\t  // call is then UNSUPPORTED) rather than risk a wrong-width/wrong-value test.\n320\t  if (unsigned n = parse_fixed_bytes_width(sol_type))\n321\t    return format_fixed_bytes(n, value);\n322\t\n323\t  // Dynamic `bytes`: recovered as a BytesDynamic struct\n324\t  // {offset,length,capacity,initialized,…}. The byte CONTENT lives in a\n325\t  // separate pool addressed by `offset` and is not faithfully recoverable, but\n326\t  // the `.length` field is — and a branch on a `bytes` argument reads it via\n327\t  // `.length`. It is filled\n// at instrumentation time and costs no query.\n#include <goto-programs/goto_coverage.h>\n#include <ac_config.h>\n#include <util/prefix.h>\n#include <util/mp_arith.h>\n#include <util/message/format.h>\n#include <util/std_code.h>\n#include <util/std_expr.h>\n#include <irep2/irep2_expr.h>\n#include <fstream>\n#include <functional>\n#include <sstream>\n#include <set>\n#include <unordered_set>\n#include <algorithm>\n#include <cctype>\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Symbol-name parsing\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nbool foundry_generator::parse_param_symbol(\n  const std::string &raw,\n  std::string &contract,\n  std::string &method,\n  std::string &param)\n{\n  // Strip SSA level/renaming suffixes: keep the base identifier only.\n  std::string name = raw;\n  size_t cut = name.find_first_of(\"?!&#\");\n  if (cut != std::string::npos)\n    name.resize(cut);\n\n  // Solidity function parameters are named\n  // `sol:@C@<contract>@F@<method>@<param>`.\n  const std::string pfx = \"sol:@C@\";\n  if (!has_prefix(name, pfx))\n    return false;\n  std::string rest = name.substr(pfx.size());\n\n  size_t f = rest.find(\"@F@\");\n  if (f == std::string::npos)\n    return false;\n  contract = rest.substr(0, f);\n  std::string after = rest.substr(f + 3);\n\n  size_t a = after.find('@');\n  if (a == std::string::npos)\n    return false;\n  method = after.substr(0, a);\n  param = after.substr(a + 1);\n\n  // A genuine parameter is a single trailing identifier (no further scope\n  // separators). A fixed\n// bytesN lowers to the `BytesStatic` struct (its `#sol_type` is the tag\n// \"BytesStatic\"); when the source width survives as `#sol_bytesn_size`\n// (set in get_elementary_type_name, solidity_convert_type.cpp) it is recovered\n// as \"BYTES<N>\" so the value formatter can render the exact-width literal. Handle both; the callee is the function operand.\n  const exprt *callee = nullptr;\n  if (e.is_code() && to_code(e).get_statement() == \"function_call\")\n    callee = &to_code_function_call(to_code(e)).function();\n  else if (\n    e.id() == \"sideeffect\" && e.get(\"statement\") == \"function_call\" &&\n    !e.operands().empty())\n    callee = &e.op0();\n\n  if (callee && callee->id() == \"symbol\")\n  {\n    const std::string id = callee->get(\"identifier\").as_string();\n    if (has_prefix(id, cpfx))\n    {\n      std::string rest = id.substr(cpfx.size());\n      size_t h = rest.find('#');\n      std::string base = h == std::string::npos ? rest : rest.substr(0, h);\n      if (\n        !base.empty() && base[0] != '_' && base[0] != '$' &&\n        base.find('@') == std::string::npos)\n      {\n        auto &v = calls[base];\n        if (std::find(v.begin(), v.end(), id) == v.end())\n          v.push_back(id);\n      }\n    }\n  }\n  forall_operands (op, e)\n    collect_dispatch_calls(*op, cpfx, calls);\n}\n\nconst std::map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> &\nfoundry_generator::dispatcher_callable(\n  const namespacet &ns,\n  const std::string &contract) const\n{\n  auto it = dispatcher_methods.find(contract);\n  if (it != dispatcher_methods.end())\n    return it->second;\n\n  std::map<std::string, std::vector<std::string>> calls;\n  const std::string disp_id =\n    \"sol:@C@\" + contract + \"@_ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_\" + contract + \"#\";\n  if (const symbolt *disp = ns.lookup(irep_idt(disp_id)))\n    collect_dispatch_calls(disp->value, \"sol:@C@\" + contract + \"@F@\", calls);\n\n  return dispatcher_methods.emplace(contract, std::move(calls)).first->second;\n}\n\n// Whether Solidity forbids `new` on this contract (abstract / interface /\n// library). Returns the callable method, or \"\" when `name`\n  // is neither callable nor a wrapper of a callable method.\n  auto resolve_dispatcher_method =\n    [&](const std::string &contract, const std::string &name) -> std::string {\n    const auto &callable = dispatcher_callable(ns, contract);\n    if (callable.count(name))\n      return name;\n    if (\n      const symbolt *s =\n        ns.lookup(irep_idt(\"sol:@C@\" + contract + \"@F@\" + name + \"#0\")))\n    {\n      const std::string real =\n        s->type.get(\"#sol_modifier_wrapper_for\").as_string();\n      if (!real.empty() && callable.count(real))\n      {\n        // Guard against the frontend's unescaped `<method>_<modifier>` wrapper\n        // naming: `a`+modifier `b_mod` and `a_b`+modifier `mod` both produce\n        // wrapper `a_b_mod`, collapsing to one symbol whose single stamp may\n        // name the wrong sibling. A U cell that can also absorb an implementation\n195\t  // defect makes that claim false — and it has absorbed one three times already\n196\t  // (ordinal-key mismatch, the RETURN exit, `rawBalances`). Each time the broken\n197\t  // case was indistinguishable from an honest solver timeout, because \"we do not\n198\t  // know\" is a legitimate, expected outcome.\n199\t  //\n200\t  // So every U must be classifiable, and a U that is not is a HARD FAILURE\n201\t  // rather than a quiet residue. The tokens:\n202\t  //\n203\t  //   named-obstacle      the unit is disqualified (the model admits an\n204\t  //                       execution the chain does not have). Not an unknown at\n205\t  //                       all — a declared exclusion that no verdict can change.\n206\t  //   bounded-holds       the solver proved no witness AT THIS EXPLORATION.\n207\t  //                       Honest and precise: it is not \"unreachable\", it is\n208\t  //                       \"no witness within the declared tx/unwind bound from\n209\t  //                       the post-constructor entry state\".\n210\t  //   solver-unknown      the solver returned UNKNOWN/error, or an inductive\n211\t  //                       step could not prove it. The genuine \"we do not know\".\n212\t  //   not-solved-this-run the claim was instrumented but never reached the\n213\t  //                       solver. The entry-liveness audit catches the case\n214\t  //                       where a WHOLE unit is in this state; this token is\n215\t  //                       exactly the per-claim residue it cannot see.\n216\t  //   unit-not-entered    the harness never entered this path's unit, so no\n217\t  //                       classification of the path itself means anything.\n218\t  //\n219\t  // ORDER MATTERS, and `unit-not-entered` must sit SECOND — directly under\n220\t  // named-obstacle and ABOVE the two tokens that would otherwise swallow it:\n221\t  //\n222\t  //   * a unit that is entered but whose claims hold vacuously gets verdict 'P'\n223\t  //     and would be filed `bounded-holds` — \"no witness within the bound\",\n224\t  //     which is a statement about the path when the truth is that nothing ran;\n225\t  //   * a unit whose claims were never generated at all (measured on a real\n226\t  //     benchmark: 120166 instrumented paths, ZERO verification conditions) has\n227\t  //     no verdict and would be filed `not-solved-this-run`.\n228\t  //\n229\t  // Both are strictly less informative than the real reason, so putting them\n230\t  // first loses the one fact worth having. The ordering rule is the same one\n231\t  // that puts named-obstacle at the top: when the unit is disqualified, or was\n232\t  // never entered, every finer classification of its paths is meaningless.\n233\t  //\n234\t  // This is NOT a reserved slot — it fires today. With --focus-function the\n235\t  // audit deliberately does not abort for the units the narrowing excluded, so\n236\t  // their paths reach the report; measured before the ordering was fixed, they\n237\t  // were all reported `not-solved-this-run` on a run whose own log line one\n238\t  // line earlier said the unit had not been entered.\n239\t  //\n240\t  // This is an INVARIANT ASSERTION, not a detector: the live tokens partition\n241\t  // the possible states by construction (a claim's verdict is one of\n242\t  // {none, P, U, F}, and F means witnessed, hence not U). It therefore needs no\n243\t  // fault injection — its value is as a tripwire for a future change that\n244\t  // introduces a U with no reason. THE PARTITION ARGUMENT ONLY HOLDS WHILE THE\n245\t  // CLASSIFICATION HAS NO CATCH-ALL: the implementation's `default` arm returns\n246\t  // \"\" so the caller aborts. Every path was then reported \"U\", which is indistinguishable from an\n264\t  // honest solver timeout, so a completely empty run looked like a merely hard\n265\t  // one. Nothing crashed and nothing warned; the defect was found by a human\n266\t  // reading a log line.\n267\t  //\n268\t  // Two levels of the same failure, deliberately sharing ONE channel so that\n269\t  // implementing half of it cannot leave the other half silent:\n270\t  //   * a unit whose claims never reached the solver was never entered;\n271\t  //   * zero verification conditions overall is the extreme case of that, where\n272\t  //     EVERY unit was never entered.\n273\t  //\n274\t  // The witness is positive: a claim that produced a solver verdict proves the\n275\t  // unit was executed. In particular --solidity-max-tx 0\n333\t  //         does NOT: coverage rewrites the dispatcher back-edge to a SKIP, so\n334\t  //         that flag explores ONE transaction — fewer than\n335\t  //         --solidity-max-tx 2. Every 'P' is therefore reported as U with\n336\t  //         `bounded_holds: true`. See path_cov_can_prove_unreachable() in\n337\t  //         bmc.cpp, which is the single place to change if a havoc'd-entry or\n338\t  //         loop-live exploration mode is ever added.\n339\t  //   'U' — undecided: solver UNKNOWN/error, or the inductive step could\n340\t  //         not prove it.\n341\t  // Written under a mutex (--parallel-solving runs jobs on threads).\n342\t  static std::map<std::string, char> claim_outcome;\n343\t  static std::mutex claim_outcome_mutex;\n344\t\n345\t  // Complete paths whose exit is a detected custom-error revert\n346\t  // (`revert E()` reaching a `#sol_error` call). Harness plumbing\n477\t    // (allocator tables, dispatcher choice bits, temporaries) is NOT an input\n478\t    // and is counted in `dropped_internal` instead of polluting this list.\n479\t    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> inputs;\n480\t    // EVM environment the path was witnessed under (msg.*/tx.*/block.*),\n481\t    // kept separate because it is context, not an argument.\n482\t    std::vector<std::pair<std::string, std::string>> env;\n483\t    // How many nondet values were classified as harness-internal and dropped.\n484\t    // Reported so the omission is visible rather than silent.\n485\t    size_t dropped_internal = 0;\n486\t    // What the external calls on this path RETURNED. The box\n  //     is a containment statement per coordinate; one missing coordinate costs\n  //     information, not correctness. It must never be treated as a measured\n  //     `[0, TYPE_MAX]` bound for THIS path, which would widen this path's own\n  //     region and break the only-ever-narrower invariant.","numLines":400,"startLine":500,"totalLines":991}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"cfaeaf78-c997-4a95-8d0f-e3a000a0e35b","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/samson/workspace/paper_review","sessionId":"e0047351-2714-4000-919d-058ca8af97c5","version":"2.1.220","gitBranch":"VeriPUT","slug":"synchronous-wondering-flame"}

\"msg.value\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bmsg_sig\\b)\"), \"msg.sig\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bmsg_data\\b)\"), \"msg.data\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\btx_origin\\b)\"), \"tx.origin\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\btx_gasprice\\b)\"), \"tx.gasprice\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_number\\b)\"), \"block.number\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_timestamp\\b)\"), \"block.timestamp\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_coinbase\\b)\"), \"block.coinbase\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_difficulty\\b)\"), \"block.difficulty\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_gaslimit\\b)\"), \"block.gaslimit\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_chainid\\b)\"), \"block.chainid\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_basefee\\b)\"), \"block.basefee\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_blobbasefee\\b)\"), \"block.blobbasefee\"},\n    {std::regex(R\"(\\bblock_prevrandao\\b)\"), \"block.prevrandao\"},\n  };\n  for (const auto &[re, repl] : name_map)\n    s = std::regex_replace(s, re, repl);\n\n  // Remove redundant parentheses left by cast removal, e.g. ((x)) -> (x)\n  // Iteratively reduce until stable (handles nested cases)\n  static const std::regex double_paren(R\"(\\((\\([^()]*\\))\\))\");\n  std::string prev;\n  do\n  {\n    prev = s;\n    s = std::regex_replace(s, double_paren, \"$1\");\n  } while (s != prev);\n\n  // Remove parens in array exploration over-approximated every reachable\n// state. Nothing in Solidity coverage mode does:\n//\n//  * `--solidity-max-tx N` with N > 0 emits N straight-line transactions —\n//    bounded by construction.\n//  * `--solidity-max-tx 0` asks the frontend for the `while (nondet_bool())\n//    dispatch()` driver, which READS as unbounded — but that loop is then\n//    destroyed. esbmc_parseoptions.cpp::process_goto_program walks every\n//    function whose name contains `_ESBMC_Main` and calls make_skip() on each\n//    `is_backwards_goto()`, under a condition (`is_coverage &&\n//    !--coverage-multi-tx`) whose `is_coverage` disjunction includes\n//    `--solidity-path-coverage`. One guarded transaction is left, so max_tx 0\n//    is the SHALLOWEST setting, not an unbounded one.\n//\n//    Verified three independent ways, not taken from documentation:\n//      - the code above;\n//      - `--show-loops` on the same contract lists `_ESBMC_Main_S` as a loop\n//        WITHOUT the coverage flag and does not list it WITH it (every other\n//        loop identical);\n//      - behaviour: on `arm(); fire();`, where fire()'s guarded path needs a\n//        prior transaction, that path is REACHED at --solidity-max-tx 2 and\n//        NOT reached at --solidity-max-tx 0.\n//  * the entry state is whatever the constructor left; state variables are\n//    never havoc'd, so an UNSAT only says \"not reachable from THIS entry\n//    state\", not \"not reachable\".\n//\n// Treating max_tx == 0 as unbounded — which this code used to do — would dress\n// a one-transaction budget up as a proof of unreachability, the exact failure\n// the tri-state exists to prevent. exploration mode exists, this is the single place to change.\nstatic bool path_cov_can_prove_unreachable()\n{\n  return false;\n}\n\n// Parse location string \"file X line Y column Z function F\" into components\nstatic nlohmann::json parse_claim_location(const std::string &loc)\n{\n  nlohmann::json j;\n  j[\"file\"] = \"\";\n  j[\"line\"] = 0;\n  j[\"column\"] = 0;\n  j[\"function\"] = \"\";\n\n  std::istringstream iss(loc);\n  std::string token;\n  while (iss >> token)\n  {\n    if (token == \"file\")\n    {\n      std::string val;\n      iss >> val;\n      j[\"file\"] = val;\n    }\n    else j[\"column\"] = val;\n    }\n    else if (token == \"function\")\n    {\n      std::string val;\n      iss >> val;\n      j[\"function\"] = val;\n    }\n  }\n  return j;\n}\n\nvoid report_coverage(\n &ctest_gen,\n  foundry_generator &foundry_gen)\n{\n  bool is_assert_cov = options.get_bool_option(\"assertion-coverage\") ||\n options.get_bool_option(\"condition-coverage-claims\") ||\n                     options.get_bool_option(\"condition-coverage-rm\") ||\n                     options.get_bool_option(\"condition-coverage-claims-rm\");\n  bool is_branch_cov = options.get_bool_option(\"branch-coverage\") ||\n Goals reachable \"\n        \"only through those paths are counted as uncovered. Raise --unwind, \"\n        \"use --unwindset/--unwindsetname for the specific loop, or switch to \"\n        \"--k-induction / --incremental-bmc. Loops truncated:\",\n        goto_functionst::truncated_loops.size());\n      for (const auto &l : goto_functionst::truncated_loops)\n        log_warning(\"  {}\", l);\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (is_assert_cov)\n  {\n    const int total = goto_coveraget::total_assert;\n    const int tracked_instance = reached_mul_claims.size();\n    const int total_instance = goto_coveraget::total_assert_ins;\n\n    log_success(\"\\n[Coverage]\\n\");\n    // The total assertion instances include the assert inside the source file, the unwinding asserts, the claims inserted during the goto-check and so on.\n    log_result(\"Total Asserts: {}\", total);\n    if (total_instance >= tracked_instance)\n      log_result(\"Total Assertion Instances: {}\", total_instance);\n    else\n      // this could be\n      // 1. the loop is too large that we cannot goto-unwind it\n      // 2. the loop is somewhat non-deterministic that we cannot run goto-unwind\n An untokened U is that claim being false, \"\n1287\t            \"and it is exactly the shape in which an implementation defect \"\n1288\t            \"hides inside an honest-looking 'we do not know'.\",\n1289\t            untokened.size(),\n1290\t            names);\n1291\t          abort();\n1292\t        }\n1293\t      }\n1294\t    }\n1295\t\n1296\t    // Final write-back of the CONTENT-ADDRESSED cover.\n1297\t    //\n1298\t    // This call was missing, and the omission killed the whole cross-run\n1299\t    // mechanism silently. `write_path_covered_set_atomic` existed and was\n1300\t    // correct; nothing called it, while the code here called the BRANCH\n1301\t    // metric's writer, gated on `covered_set_outpath` — which\n1302\t    // solidity_path_coverage() never sets. Measured before the fix: running\n1303\t    // with `--coverage-covered-set cov.json` produced no file at all, so every\n1304\t    // round re-instrumented everything and the escalation story (round N spends\n1305\t    // its budget only on paths still lacking a CE) did not work at all.\n1306\t    //\n1307\t    // Same defect shape as the entry-liveness audit before it was wired: a\n1308\t    // function that is written, tested by eye, and never called. The function\n1309\t    // itself selects only 'F' claims, so nothing but a real witness is ever\n1310\t    // persisted.\n1311\t    if (cov_set_active)\n1312\t    {\n1313\t      goto_coveraget::write_path_covered_set_atomic();\n1314\t      log_success(\n1315\t        \"coverage covered-set written to {}\",\n1316\t        goto_coveraget::path_covered_outpath);\n1317\t    }\n1318\t    } // end of the non-certification reporting block\n1319\t  }\n1320\t\n1321\t  // Generate JSON coverage report\n1322\t  if (options.get_bool_option(\"cov-report-json\"))\n1323\t  {\n1324\t    using json = nlohmann::json;\n1325\t\n1326\t    std::string cov_type = \"unknown\";\n1327\t    if (is_branch_cov)\n1328\t      cov_type = \"branch\";\n1329\t    else if (is_branch_func_cov)\n1330\t      cov_type = \"branch-function\";\n1331\t    else if (is_k_path_cov)\n1332\t      cov_type = \"k-path\";\n1333\t    else if (is_path_cov)\n1334\t      cov_type = \"solidity-path\";\n1335\t    else if (is_cond_cov)\n1336\t      cov_type = \"condition\";\n1337\t    else if (is_assert_cov)\n1338\t      cov_type = \"assertion\";\n1339\t\n1340\t    const auto &all_claims = goto_coveraget::all_claims;\n1341\t    std::set<std::string> source_files;\n1342\t    json claims_json = json::array();\n1343\t\n1344\t    // Bound under which THIS run's verdicts were produced. Recorded on every\n1345\t    // path entry: a \"holds\" verdict is only meaningful together with the\n1346\t    // exploration it was obtained under.\n1347\t    const std::string max_tx = options.get_option(\"solidity-max-tx\");\n1348\t    const std::string unwind_s = options.get_option(\"unwind\");\n1349\t    bool loops_truncated = false;\n1350\t    {\n1351\t      std::lock_guard lk(goto_functionst::truncated_loops_mutex);\n1352\t      loops_truncated = !goto_functionst::truncated_loops.empty();\n1353\t    }\n1354\t    // See path_cov_can_prove_unreachable(). This used to be\n1355\t    // `max_tx == \"0\" && !loops_truncated`, on the belief that max_tx 0 gives an\n1356\t    // unbounded transaction sequence. It does not: coverage rewrites the\n1357\t    // dispatcher back-edge to a SKIP, so max_tx 0 explores ONE transaction —\n1358\t    // fewer than max_tx 2. Every non-refuted path is therefore U.\n1359\t    const bool unbounded_run = path_cov_can_prove_unreachable();\n1360\t    // What the transaction driver ACTUALLY explored, stated on every entry so a\n1361\t    // reader never has to infer it from the flag. `--solidity-max-tx 0` is the\n1362\t    // trap: it reads as \"unbounded\" and is in fact the shallowest setting.\n1363\t    const std::string tx_exploration =\n1364\t      max_tx == \"0\"\n1365\t        ? std::string(\n1366\t            \"one guarded transaction: --solidity-max-tx 0 emits the \"\n1367\t            \"`while (nondet) dispatch()` driver, but Solidity coverage rewrites \"\n1368\t            \"every _ESBMC_Main* back-edge to a SKIP, so the loop runs at most \"\n1369\t            \"once. This explores FEWER transactions than --solidity-max-tx 2\")\n1370\t        : (max_tx.empty()\n1371\t             ? std::string(\n1372\t                 \"coverage default: the dispatcher loop back-edge is rewritten \"\n1373\t                 \"to a SKIP, leaving one guarded transaction\")\n1374\t             : (\"exactly \" + max_tx +\n1375\t                \" straight-line transaction(s) (no dispatcher back-edge to \"\n1376\t                \"remove)\"));\n1377\t\n1378\t    for (const auto &[claim_msg, claim_loc] : all_claims)\n1379\t    {\n1380\t      std::string claim_sig = claim_msg + \"\\t\" + claim_loc;\n1381\t      bool covered = reached_claims.count(claim_sig) > 0;\n1382\t\n1383\t      // For assertion coverage, check reached_mul_claims instead\n1384\t      if (is_assert_cov)\n1385\t        covered = reached_mul_claims.count(claim_sig) > 0;\n1386\t\n1387\t      json loc = parse_claim_location(claim_loc);\n1388\t      std::string file = loc[\"file\"];\n1389\t      if (!file.empty())\n1390\t        source_files.insert(file);\n1391\t\n1392\t      json claim_entry;\n1393\t      claim_entry[\"condition\"] = prettify_solidity_expr(claim_msg);\n1394\t      claim_entry[\"file\"] = loc[\"file\"];\n1395\t      claim_entry[\"line\"] = loc[\"line\"];\n1396\t      claim_entry[\"column\"] = loc[\"column\"];\n1397\t      claim_entry[\"function\"] = loc[\"function\"];\n1398\t      claim_entry[\"status\"] = covered ? \"covered\" : \"uncovered\";\n1399\t      // k-path Phase-2 (#4335): annotate each claim as feasible (a\n1400\t      // maximal element of the subsumption lattice and thus part of the\n1401\t      // spanning set) or spanning-set-redundant (subsumed by a stronger\n1402\t      // emitted goal — covering it adds no information beyond covering\n1403\t      // its subsumer).\n1404\t      if (is_k_path_cov)\n1405\t      {\n1406\t        const auto &redundant = goto_coveraget::k_path_spanning_redundant;\n1407\t        claim_entry[\"feasibility\"] = redundant.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) > 0\n1408\t                                       ? \"spanning-set-redundant\"\n1409\t                                       : \"feasible\";\n1410\t      }\n1411\t\n1412\t      // Solidity complete-path coverage: the CE->generalisation interface.\n1413\t      // Tri-state per complete path, plus the bound the verdict was reached\n1414\t      // under and how the path exits.\n1415\t      if (is_path_cov)\n1416\t      {\n1417\t        char v = 0;\n1418\t        {\n1419\t          std::lock_guard lock(goto_coveraget::claim_outcome_mutex);\n1420\t          auto it_o = goto_coveraget::claim_outcome.find(claim_sig);\n1421\t          if (it_o != goto_coveraget::claim_outcome.end())\n1422\t            v = it_o->second;\n1423\t        }\n1424\t        // Witnessed = refuted this run, or already refuted in an earlier\n1425\t        // escalation round (cross-run covered-set). Either way a concrete\n1426\t        // input exists for this path.\n1427\t        const bool prior =\n1428\t          goto_coveraget::path_witnessed_earlier({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n1429\t        const bool witnessed = covered || prior;\n1430\t\n1431\t        // F: feasible, CE in hand.\n1432\t        // I: PROVEN unreachable. No coverage configuration can establish this\n1433\t        //    today — see path_cov_can_prove_unreachable() — so this arm is\n1434\t        //    currently unreachable by construction, deliberately.\n1435\t        // U: everything else, INCLUDING a claim that \"holds\" at this\n1436\t        //    exploration: that means no witness within one-or-N transactions\n1437\t        //    from the post-constructor entry state, not that the path is\n1438\t        //    unreachable. It stays U and is flagged `bounded_holds`.\n1439\t        std::string tri;\n1440\t        if (witnessed)\n1441\t          tri = \"F\";\n1442\t        else if (v == 'P' && unbounded_run)\n1443\t          tri = \"I\";\n1444\t        else\n1445\t          tri = \"U\";\n1446\t        claim_entry[\"status\"] = tri;\n1447\t        if (tri == \"U\")\n1448\t        {\n1449\t          // Same single source as the stdout breakdown, so the file and the\n1450\t          // terminal can never disagree about why a path is uncovered.\n1451\t          const std::string tok =\n1452\t            goto_coveraget::path_u_reason_token({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n1453\t          claim_entry[\"u_reason\"] = tok;\n1454\t          if (tok == \"named-obstacle\")\n1455\t          {\n1456\t            auto ob =\n1457\t              goto_coveraget::named_obstacle_paths.find({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n1458\t            if (ob != goto_coveraget::named_obstacle_paths.end())\n1459\t              claim_entry[\"u_reason_detail\"] = ob->second;\n1460\t          }\n1461\t          else if (tok == \"unit-not-entered\")\n1462\t          {\n1463\t            // WHY the unit was not entered, not just that it wasn't: excluded\n1464\t            // on purpose by --focus-function is a normal per-method run, while\n1465\t            // \"the harness never entered it\" is a defect. A consumer that\n1466\t            // cannot tell them apart would treat a deliberate narrowing as a\n1467\t            // broken run, or worse, the reverse.\n1468\t            const size_t p = claim_msg.rfind(\":path:\");\n1469\t            const std::string unit =\n1470\t              p == std::string::npos ? claim_msg : claim_msg.substr(0, p);\n1471\t            auto ue = goto_coveraget::units_not_entered.find(unit);\n1472\t            if (ue != goto_coveraget::units_not_entered.end())\n1473\t              claim_entry[\"u_reason_detail\"] = ue->second;\n1474\t          }\n1475\t        }\n1476\t        // Kept alongside the token: a consumer that already reads these keys\n1477\t        // keeps working, and `bounded_holds` additionally marks the U's worth\n1478\t        // re-checking under a deeper exploration.\n1479\t        if (v == 'P' && !unbounded_run)\n1480\t          claim_entry[\"bounded_holds\"] = true;\n1481\t        if (!witnessed && v == 0)\n1482\t          // Never handed to the solver this run (sliced away, or skipped\n1483\t          // because an earlier round already covered a different path).\n1484\t          claim_entry[\"not_solved_this_run\"] = true;\n1485\t\n1486\t        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"max_tx\"] = max_tx.empty() ? \"default\" : max_tx;\n1487\t        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"unwind\"] =\n1488\t          unwind_s.empty() ? \"default\" : unwind_s;\n1489\t        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"kind\"] = unbounded_run ? \"unbounded\" : \"bounded\";\n1490\t        claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"tx_exploration\"] = tx_exploration;\n1491\t        if (loops_truncated)\n1492\t          claim_entry[\"bound\"][\"loops_truncated\"] = true;\n1493\t        // Both revert shapes exit the transaction, so both are \"revert\": the\n1494\t        // custom-error one (ASSUME(false) in a #sol_error callee) and the\n1495\t        // rollback one (require/revert(\"msg\"), which restores `*this` and then\n1496\t        // reaches END_FUNCTION). Reporting the latter as \"normal\" would claim a\n1497\t        // reverting transaction succeeded.\n1498\t        const bool ck_err =\n1499\t          goto_coveraget::revert_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) > 0;\n1500\t        const bool ck_rb =\n1501\t          goto_coveraget::rollback_revert_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) >\n1502\t          0;\n1503\t        const bool ck_un =\n1504\t          goto_coveraget::undetermined_exit_paths.count({claim_msg, claim_loc}) >\n1505\t          0;\n1506\t        claim_entry[\"exit_kind\"] =\n1507\t          (ck_err || ck_rb) ? \"revert\" : (ck_un ? \"undetermined\" : \"normal\");\n1508\t        if (ck_rb)\n1509\t          // Distinguishes the two: here the rollback IS modelled, so\n1510\t          // final_state is the correctly restored post-state.\n1511\t          claim_entry[\"revert_kind\"] = \"rollback\";\n1512\t        else if (ck_err)\n1513\t          claim_entry[\"revert_kind\"] = \"custom-error\";\n1514\t        else if (ck_un)\n1515\t          claim_entry[\"exit_kind_undetermined_reason\"] =\n1516\t            \"reaches END_FUNCTION bypassing the function epilogue and carries \"\n1517\t            \"no rollback restore: a `require` failing before any state write \"\n1518\t            \"and a plain early `return` compile to the same shape, so this is \"\n1519\t            \"either a revert or a normal early exit\";\n1520\t        claim_entry[\"witnessed_in_earlier_round\"] = prior && !covered;\n1521\t\n1522\t        // path_id == enc(pi): the integer encoding the path's whole decision\n1523\t        // sequence (tr accumulator). Text before \":path:\" is the function.\n1524\t        const auto pos = claim_msg.rfind(\":path:\");\n1525\t        if (pos != std::string::npos)\n1526\t        {\n1527\t          claim_entry[\"path_id\"] = claim_msg.substr(pos + 6);\n1528\t          claim_entry[\"path_function\"] = claim_msg.substr(0, pos);\n1529\t        }\n1530\t        // The decision depth, i.e. the `cnt` half of the path's identity. A\n1531\t        // stage-2 query is `tr == enc && cnt == depth`, so a consumer that only\n1532\t        // had `path_id` could not build one; it had to be told the depth out of\n1533\t        // band, which is the opposite of an interface.\n1534\t        {\n1535\t          auto dp =\n1536\t            goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.find({claim_msg, claim_loc});\n1537\t          if (dp != goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.end())\n1538\t            claim_entry[\"path_depth\"] = dp->second;\n1539\t\n1540\t          // ---- THE ORDERED DECISION SEQUENCE, for F claims only ----\n1541\t          //\n1542\t          // This is what makes path coverage comparable with branch coverage at\n1543\t          // all: the two metrics share no denominator until the witnessed paths\n1544\t          // are projected onto the DECISIONS they walk. `path_id` cannot be\n1545\t          // projected — `enc` records the arms and nothing about the sites, so\n1546\t          // only the enumerator knows which instruction each bit came from.\n1547\t          //\n1548\t          // RESTRICTED TO F on purpose, and it is not merely a saving. F is the\n1549\t          // only status the projection can use (an uncovered path witnesses no\n1550\t          // decision), and F is rare — single digits per unit — while a unit can\n1551\t          // enumerate 120166 paths. Emitting for every claim would put the\n1552\t          // report's size in the same order as the path count for no gain.\n1553\t          if (tri == \"F\" && pos != std::string::npos)\n1554\t          {\n1555\t            const std::string unit = claim_msg.substr(0, pos);\n1556\t            const uint64_t penc =\n1557\t              strtoull(claim_msg.substr(pos + 6).c_str(), nullptr, 10);\n1558\t            auto ti = goto_coveraget::path_decision_table.find(unit);\n1559\t            auto xi = goto_coveraget::path_decision_index.find(unit);\n1560\t            if (\n1561\t              ti != goto_coveraget::path_decision_table.end() &&\n1562\t              xi != goto_coveraget::path_decision_index.end() &&\n1563\t              dp != goto_coveraget::path_decision_depth.end() &&\n1564\t              dp->second > 0)\n1565\t            {\n1566\t              const uint64_t pdepth = dp->second;\n1567\t              json seq = json::array();\n1568\t              size_t missing = 0;\n1569\t              for (uint64_t k = 0; k < pdepth; ++k)\n1570\t              {\n1571\t                const uint64_t key = penc >> (pdepth - 1 - k);\n1572\t                auto di = xi->second.find(key);\n1573\t                if (di == xi->second.end() || di->second >= ti->second.size())\n1574\t                {\n1575\t                  // Reported as a hole, never skipped. A shorter array would\n1576\t                  // read as \"this path walks fewer decisions\" — a claim about\n1577\t                  // the path, when the truth is a claim about the recording.\n1578\t                  json h;\n1579\t                  h[\"index\"] = k + 1;\n1580\t                  h[\"unrecorded_prefix_enc\"] = std::to_string(key);\n1581\t                  seq.push_back(h);\n1582\t                  ++missing;\n1583\t                  continue;\n1584\t                }\n1585\t                const auto &d = ti->second[di->second];\n1586\t                const bool arm_taken = (key & 1) != 0;\n1587\t                json e;\n1588\t                e[\"index\"] = k + 1;\n1589\t                json dloc = parse_claim_location(d.loc);\n1590\t                e[\"file\"] = dloc[\"file\"];\n1591\t                e[\"line\"] = dloc[\"line\"];\n1592\t                e[\"column\"] = dloc[\"column\"];\n1593\t                e[\"function\"] = dloc[\"function\"];\n1594\t                e[\"operand\"] = d.sub;\n1595\t                e[\"arm\"] = arm_taken ? \"taken\" : \"fall-through\";\n1596\t                // This arm's claim text, already inverted (assert(P) fails when\n1597\t                // P is false, so assert(guard) covers the FALL-THROUGH edge).\n1598\t                // Published rather than left to the consumer: inverting it\n1599\t                // there is a silent error that still produces a number.\n1600\t                //\n1601\t                // DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — do not join on it. Measured: a `require`\n1602\t                // lowers to a guard one `not` deeper under path coverage than\n1603\t                // under branch coverage (the revert-observation gate), so the\n1604\t                // texts differ for the same decision while a plain `if` agrees\n1605\t                // verbatim. See path_decisiont in goto_coverage.h. Join on\n1606\t                // file+line, which is the comparison metric's own unit.\n1607\t                e[\"branch_claim\"] = prettify_solidity_expr(\n1608\t                  arm_taken ? d.cond_arm_true : d.cond_arm_false);\n1609\t                if (d.synthetic_abi_gate)\n1610\t                  // No branch-coverage counterpart AND a location copied from\n1611\t                  // the unit's first body instruction, so a consumer matching on\n1612\t                  // location alone would credit a real decision on that line.\n1613\t                  e[\"synthetic_abi_gate\"] = true;\n1614\t                seq.push_back(e);\n1615\t              }\n1616\t              claim_entry[\"decisions\"] = seq;\n1617\t              if (missing > 0)\n1618\t                claim_entry[\"decisions_unrecorded\"] = missing;\n1619\t            }\n1620\t          }\n1621\t        }\n1622\t\n1623\t        // CE payload: the concrete values behind an F. Absent for I/U (there\n1624\t        // is no counterexample to report).\n1625\t        std::lock_guard lock(goto_coveraget::claim_outcome_mutex);\n1626\t        auto it_ce = goto_coveraget::path_ce.find(claim_sig);\n1627\t        if (it_ce != goto_coveraget::path_ce.end())\n1628\t        {\n1629\t          const auto &ce = it_ce->second;\n1630\t          json ins = json::object();\n1631\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.inputs)\n1632\t            ins[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n1633\t          json envj = json::object();\n1634\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.env)\n1635\t            envj[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n1636\t          json fin = json::object();\n1637\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.final_state)\n1638\t            fin[prettify_solidity_expr(n)] = v;\n1639\t          claim_entry[\"inputs\"] = ins;\n1640\t          claim_entry[\"env\"] = envj;\n1641\t          // What the outside world returned on this path, in call order. Kept\n1642\t          // separate from `inputs` because a consumer can CHOOSE an input and\n1643\t          // cannot choose this: a replay has to mock the callee to return these\n1644\t          // values. An ARRAY, not a map — repeated calls reuse the same symbol\n1645\t          // name and their order is part of the answer.\n1646\t          json ext = json::array();\n1647\t          for (const auto &[n, v] : ce.extcall_returns)\n1648\t            ext.push_back({{\"symbol\", prettify_solidity_expr(n)}, {\"value\", v}});\n1649\t          claim_entry[\"extcall_returns\"] = ext;\n1650\t          if (ce.extcall_returns.empty())\n1651\t            // NOT \"there were no external calls\": say what is actually known.\n1652\t            //\n1653\t            // This list is ALWAYS empty: nothing anywhere writes to\n1654\t            // ce.extcall_returns. Below is what stands between the value and\n1655\t            // this field, measured on a four-unit contract whose units differ\n1656\t            // ONLY in the syntactic shape the call's result arrives in. There\n1657\t            // are THREE distinct reasons, not one, and a fix for any single one\n1658\t            // leaves the field empty in the other shapes -- which looks exactly\n1659\t            // like no fix at all.\n1660\t            //\n1661\t            //   (a) result bound to a named local (`bool ok = c.f();`) and the\n1662\t            //       assembly form (`success` assigned inside an approximated\n1663\t            //       block): the step DOES reach the harvest and\n1664\t            //       get_nondet_symbol DOES resolve it. It is then dropped\n1665\t            //       because the classification below has exactly three\n1666\t            //       outcomes -- parameter -> inputs, environment -> env,\n1667\t            //       otherwise -> dropped_internal -- and a call's return is a\n1668\t            //       LOCAL, so it lands in the third. There is no bucket for it.\n1669\t            //   (b) low-level `(bool ok, ) = a.call(\"\")`: get_nondet_symbol\n1670\t            //       returns nil, so the step is skipped BEFORE classification.\n1671\t            //       (This is the mechanism an earlier version of this comment\n1672\t            //       named -- correctly, but for this shape only.)\n1673\t            //   (c) used inline (`if (c.f())`): no named local is ever\n1674\t            //       assigned, so no step carries the value at all.\n1675\t            //\n1676\t            // The _ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_* symbols that ARE in the trace are the\n1677\t            // re-entry model's method-choice bits, not the returned value\n1678\t            // (measured: identical on two paths that disagree about it), so\n1679\t            // they are deliberately not reported here.\n1680\t            claim_entry[\"ce_extraction\"][\"extcall_returns_unavailable_reason\"] =\n1681\t              \"not implemented yet, and for three different reasons depending \"\n1682\t              \"on the syntactic shape the call's result arrives in; this field \"\n1683\t              \"does NOT say which one applies to this claim. (a) bound to a \"\n1684\t              \"named local, or assigned inside an approximated assembly block: \"\n1685\t              \"the value IS harvested and resolved, then dropped because the \"\n1686\t              \"classification has buckets only for parameters and environment \"\n1687\t              \"values and a call's return is a local. (b) low-level \"\n1688\t              \"`(bool ok, ) = a.call(...)`: get_nondet_symbol returns nil, so \"\n1689\t              \"the step is skipped before classification. (c) used inline, \"\n1690\t              \"`if (c.f())`: no named local is assigned, so no trace step \"\n1691\t              \"carries it. The _ESBMC_Nondet_Extcall_* symbols that ARE in the \"\n1692\t              \"trace are the re-entry model's method-choice bits, not the \"\n1693\t              \"returned value (measured: identical on two paths that disagree \"\n1694\t              \"about it), so they are deliberately not reported here. An empty \"\n1695\t              \"list means UNKNOWN, not 'this path performs no external call'\";\n1696\t          // Contract state this path STARTED from.
